payload.gap_claim: Scanned alternatives and what each sheds. (1) MERGE EVERYTHING, today's behaviour - sheds trunk's readability: every evidence file, gate record and dead machine state lands beside the live claims and never leaves, so the working tree grows with project age. (2) SQUASH-MERGE - sheds the record entirely: one commit onto trunk with no second parent, so the branch's detail is only reachable if someone remembers the branch existed. (3) DELETE THE EVIDENCE AT CLOSE - sheds auditability outright; the ledger stops being able to answer how a decision was reached. (4) KEEP EVIDENCE IN A SEPARATE STORE outside git - sheds atomicity: the record and the claims can then disagree, and two systems must be backed up instead of one. THE CLAIM: only a merge commit that keeps both parents while filtering its own tree gets all three at once - a clean trunk, a complete record, and one storage system.
payload.why_now: Three things matured. The worktree lane exists and every iteration already runs on its own branch, so there is a branch to hold the events - that was i5 and i5b. Every tool now resolves to the open iteration's root, so work performed during an iteration actually lands in that iteration's tree rather than on trunk - committed yesterday. And the cost became concrete rather than theoretical: one ship produced zero commits, and one routine tidy-up nearly destroyed a file that existed in exactly one directory.
payload.value_props:
PROP 1 - audience: the engineer reading the ledger. Need|outcome: I open trunk and see what is true now, not the whole history of how it got true | the working tree carries live claims only. Alternative today: scrolling past ~57 evidence files per iteration. Difference: the record moves one tag away instead of underfoot. Validation signal: a close lands on trunk with zero files under an iteration's evidence or machines path. PASS LINE: after a close, git ls-tree on trunk shows no evidence/, machines/ or state.json for that iteration.

PROP 2 - audience: the engineer auditing a past decision. Need|outcome: I can still ask any shipped iteration exactly how it got there | every event stays reachable by a named handle forever. Alternative today: the branch name, if nobody cleaned it up. Difference: a mandatory tag makes the handle permanent and predictable. PASS LINE: for a closed iteration, git show iter/<id>:<evidence path> returns the file even though trunk does not have it.

PROP 3 - audience: the agent doing the work. Need|outcome: my work is durable from the first milestone | each blessed milestone commits to the iteration's branch. Alternative today: everything lives as dirty files until a close that may write nothing. Difference: losing a working directory costs nothing. PASS LINE: after a mid-iteration bless, the branch has a new commit and the working tree is clean.

PROP 4 - audience: the owner running things unattended. Need|outcome: a ship that reports success actually shipped | a close that would produce nothing refuses instead. PASS LINE: shipMerge on a branch with zero commits returns a refusal, never merged:true.
payload.business_case: Skipped with reason: no acquirer exists - this is internal engine mechanics on the owner's own tool, and the currency is the owner's own time. The measurable return is stated in the pass lines above rather than in money.
